title: CRLA/319/2013 of Bishan Lal Vs State Of Uttarakhand

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Criminal Appeal No. 319 of 2013
Bishan Lal S/o Chuhad Singh .....Appellant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand .... Respondent
Mr. Sanjeev Singh, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. S.K. Chaudhary, Addl. G.A. for the State.
Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
Present appeal is filed by assailing the judgment
and order dated 10.07.2013, passed by learned Vth
Additional Sessions Judge, Haridwar in Session Trial
No. 75 of 2006.
Brief facts of the present case, inter alia, are that
Yogendra Rathi S/o Sri Gamey Singh @ Gambhir Singh
resident of Village Isseypur, Police Station Kiratpur,
District Bijnor (U.P.) was arrested in Case Crime No. 35
of 2005, under Sections 395, 397 and 412 I.P.C., Police
Station Shyampur, District Haridwar. This Court vide
order dated 18.01.2006, passed in Bail Application No.
62 of 2006, was pleased to grant bail to Yogendra Rathi
accused. Pursuant to the bail granted by this Court vide
order dated 18.01.2006, an application was moved
before the Chief Judicial Magistrate Haridwar by
accused Yogendra Rathi through Dinesh Verma,
Advocate to release him on bail. Before the learned
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Haridwar, affidavits and
surety bonds of Chaman Singh and Bishan Lal were
produced. Mr. Dinesh Verma, Advocate has identified
Bishan Lal S/o Chuhad Singh as well as Chaman Singh
S/o Mool Singh before the learned Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Haridwar.

2
In Session Trial No. 75 of 2006, accused Yogendra
Rathi failed to appear, therefore, learned 5th Additional
Sessions Judge was pleased to issue notice to the
sureties, namely Bishan Lal S/o Chuhad Singh as well as
Chaman Singh S/o Mool Singh.
Pursuant to the notice issued by the leaned Trial
Court, Bishan Lal S/o Chuhad Singh, appellant herein
appeared before the learned Trial Court and preferred
an objection to the effect that he never stood surety for
accused Yogendra Rathi. It was further alleged that he
never produced any surety bond or affidavit before the
learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Haridwar and surety
bond and affidavit allegedly filed by the appellant did
not contain photograph and signature of the appellant
rather affidavit and surety bond were signed by the
imposter and photographs of imposter were affixed on
the surety bond and affidavit. It is further stated that
imposter was produced before the learned Chief Judicial
Magistrate instead of Bishan Lal S/o Chuhad Singh and
he was wrongly identified by Mr. Dinesh Verma,
Advocate as Bishan Lal S/o Chuhad Singh. It was
further alleged before the learned Trial Court that
earlier Mr. Dinesh Verma, Advocate was approached by
Bishan Lal S/o Chuhad Singh, appellant herein, to file
civil suit pertaining to his house for which Bishan Lal
appellant herein had provided house tax receipt and
identity proof to Mr. Dinesh Verma, Advocate.
However, later on matter was settled and there was no
need to file civil suit. Therefore, civil suit was not filed.
It was further contended that it seems that Mr. Dinesh
Verma, Advocate has produced imposter before the

3
Chief Judicial Magistrate Haridwar and has produced
the documents provided to Mr. Dinesh Verma,
Advocate.
Bishan Lal S/o Chuhad Singh is personally present
before this Court duly identified by Mr. Sanjeev Singh,
Advocate. His photograph is affixed on the affidavit
filed before this Court alongwith memo of appeal.
Appeal was taken up for hearing on 20th August, 2013.
It was contended by Mr. Sanjeev Singh, learned counsel
for the appellant, before this court that surety bond and
affidavit produced before the Chief Judicial Magisrate
Haridwar contained the photograph of Karam Singh S/o
Kalu Ram, resident of Q.No. 457, Type-2, Sector-IV,
BHEL, P.S. Ranipur, District Haridwar.
On 20.08.2013, this Court passed order as under :-
"Mr. Sanjeev Singh, Advocate for the
appellant.
 Mr. S.S. Adhikari, Brief Holder for the State.
 In the present case very interesting and
peculiar facts are involved. Yogendra Rathi
accused was directed to be released on bail. Mr.
Chaman Lal S/o Dool Singh and Mr. Bishan Lal
S/o Chuhad Singh (appellant) stood sureties for
accused Yogendra Rathi. Yogendra Rathi stopped
appearing before the Court below, therefore, non
bailable warrants were issued against him.
Police Station Shyampur, District Haridwar
reported to the Court below that accused
Yogendra Rathi left the village and was not
residing in the same village and he had sold out
his entire property situated in the village Issopur,
Post Babupura, Police Station Kiratpur, District
Bijnor. Having received such a report, notices
were issued to the sureties, i.e. Chaman Lal (3rd
party) and appellant.
It was contended before the Court below on
behalf of the appellant that he never stood surety

4
for accused Yogendra Rathi nor he ever signed
any affidavit and surety bond for securing the
release of the accused Yogendra Rathi on bail. It
was further contended before the Court below as
well as before me that affidavit does not contain
photograph of the appellant and contains the
photograph of one Karam Singh S/o Kalu Ram,
R/o Q.No. 457, Type-2, Sector IV, BHEL, P.S.
Ranipur, Haridwar.
It has further been contended by the learned
counsel for the appellant before me that in fact
appellant wanted to file injunction suit, in
connection thereof, made contact with Dinesh
Verma, Advocate of Haridwar and handed over
receipt of house tax, photocopy of identity card
and other documents. However, matter was
thereafter settled, therefore, he did not file suit for
injunction.
Mr. Sanjeev Singh, learned counsel for the
appellant contends that it seems that Mr. Dinesh
Verma, Advocate of Haridwar with the collusion
of the accused Yogendra Rathi and third person
Karam Singh, was able to submit bogus and
fabricated surety bond and affidavit of the
appellant before the Court below thereupon
affixing the photograph of Karam Singh and he
has wrongly identified Karam Singh as Bishan
Lal appellant. In fact, Karam Singh was
produced before the Court as imposter of the
appellant.
In view of the above facts and circumstances
of the case, prima-facie, it seems that perjury was
made and fraud was played on the Court below
by Mr. Dinesh Verma, Advocate and Karam
Singh. Therefore, to find out the truth, let bailable
warrant be issued against Dinesh Verma,
Advocate, having enrolment No. 618/02,
practicing at Sessions Court Haridwar through
Chief Judicial Magistrate Haridwar to remain
present in person before this Court on 9th
September, 2013. Let bailable warrant also be
issued against Mr. Karam Singh S/o Kalu Ram,
R/o Q.No. 457, Type-2, Sector IV, BHEL, P.S.

5
Ranipur, Haridwar to remain present in person
before this Court on 9th September, 2013.
Appellant shall also remain present before
this Court on 9th September, 2013.
Both the noticee shall file their respective
affidavits showing cause as to why criminal
prosecution be not initiated against them for
furnishing fabricated document before the court
below for the offences punishable under Sections
195, 420 and 471 I.P.C.
List on 9th September, 2013.
Meanwhile, operation and effect of the
impugned judgment shall remain stayed. "
Appeal was taken up on 09.09.2013. Mr. Dinesh
Verma, Advocate and Bishan Lal, present appellant
appeared before this Court on 09.09.2013. This Court
passed order on 09.09.2013 which reads as under :-
"Mr. Sanjeev Singh, Advocate for the
appellant.
Mr. S.K. Chaudhary, Addl. GA for the State.
Mr. Narendra Bali, Advocate for Mr. Dinesh
Verma, Advocate.
Appellant Bishan Lal is present, in person,
before this Court and he is duly identified by Mr.
Sanjeev Singh, Advocate.
Mr. Dinesh Verma, Advocate, is also present,
in person, before this Court and he is duly
identified by Mr. Narendra Bali, Advocate.
Looking at appellant Bishan Lal, Mr. Dinesh
Verma, Advocate stated before me that Bishan Lal
never came to him and he never identified him,
rather it seems that person whose photo is affixed
on the affidavit (paper no. 15) came to him as
impostor of Bishan Lal and believing him, he
identified him as Bishan Lal.
Despite bailable warrant issued against
Karam Singh, he is not present before this Court.
Let non bailable warrant be issued against
Karam Singh, son of Kalu Ram, resident of
quarter no. 457, Type 2, Sector IV, BHEL, police
station Ranipur, Haridwar through Chief Judicial

6
Magistrate, Haridwar. He shall be produced
before this Court on 24.10.2013.
Appellant as well as Mr. Dinesh Verma,
Advocate, shall also remain present before this
Court on the next date fixed.
Mr. Dinesh Verma shall also file his show
cause by the next date fixed.
Let original record of bail application moved
on behalf of Yogendra Rathi and bonds and
affidavits filed by the sureties be sent to this court
under a seal cover.
List on 24.10.2013."
Mr. Dinesh Verma, Advocate did not file any reply
to the show cause. He is personally present before me,
duly identified by Mr. Narendra Bali, Advocate.
Appellant is also present in person duly identified by
Mr. Sanjeev Singh, Advocate for the appellant. Karam
Singh is also present in person duly identified by Mr.
Manish Arora, Advocate.
On being asked, Mr. Dinesh Verma, Advocate
stated before me that in fact appellant is a Bishan Lal.
He, however, stated that by mistake, he had identified
the imposter as the appellant. Further stated that since
imposter claimed himself as the appellant, therefore,
had wrongly identified imposter as Bishan Lal, trusting
and believing that infact imposter was Bishan Lal. Mr.
Dinesh Verma, Advocate further stated before me that
he does not know the person whose photograph is
available on the affidavit filed before the C.J.M.
alongwith bail bond. He, however, admits that
photograph available on the affidavit alongwith surety
bond is not of Bishan Lal who is personally present
before this Court.

7
Mr. Manish Arora, Advocate submitted that
affidavit and surety bond do not contain photograph of
Karam Singh. I have compared photograph available on
the affidavit filed before the Chief Judicial Magistrate
alongwith the surety bond and it does not resemble with
Karam Singh. Therefore, Karam Singh is exonerated.
He need not to appear.
I have compared the alleged photograph of present
appellant on the affidavit and surety bond produced
before learned C.J.M. It can very well be said
photograph available on the file of C.J.M. is not of
present appellant. Moreover, signature on the affidavit
and surety bond are not of present appellant.
In the impugned order, learned Trial Court has
wrongly observed that photograph available on the
affidavit filed alongwith surety bond before the C.J.M. is
of Bishan Lal. It seems that learned Trial Judge did not
care to compare the photograph available on the
affidavit with the Bishan Lal who was personally present
before the learned trial court. The approach adopted by
the learned Trial Judge cannot be appreciated from any
angle. His attitude is totally irresponsible and uncalled
for. Judicial Officer is required to be more vigilant and
careful while discharging judicial duty because for his
negligence or casual approach innocent should not
suffer.
In view of the fact that Bishan Lal, appellant
herein, did not stood surety for Yogendra Rathi, no
recovery can be made from him.
It is not denied by Mr. Dinesh Verma, Advocate
that appellant never visited him and handed over some

8
documents to him to file civil suit, as claimed by the
appellant. Therefore, in the opinion of this Court, Mr.
Dinesh Verma, Advocate has intentionally identified
imposter as of appellant and has intentionally played
fraud on the Court by filing affidavit and surety bond
before the C.J.M. knowing well same did not contain
photograph and signature of present appellant.
Therefore, Mr. Dinesh Verma, Advocate seems to be
guilty for perjury, forgery and playing fraud on the
Court. Therefore, Registrar (Judicial) of this Court is
directed to lodge an F.I.R. against Mr. Dinesh Verma,
Advocate as well as unknown person whose photograph
is affixed on the affidavit and surety bond produced
before the Chief Judicial Magistrate as of the appellant.
In view of the above, present appeal stands
allowed. Impugned order stands quashed qua the
appellant Bishan Lal.
Let copy of this judgment be placed before the
Hon'ble the Chief Justice to take appropriate decision
against the trial Judge in administrative side.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
Dated 24th Ocot0ber, 2013 Shiv
